title: Formation of the Hebrew Bible
summary: The Hebrew Bible is an assemblage of writings dating from about 1000 BCE down to the 160s BCE. The Torah came from a long process of editing, with most scholars placing its final major edits after 539 BCE. It probably reached fixed, authoritative status first, then the Prophets and finally the Writings. By the end of the first century all of this was probably organized.

uncertainty.note: Major redaction of the Torah occurred in the Persian period (539–c. 330 BCE) with the latest biblical book (Daniel) composed in the 160s BCE during the Hellenistic era.

as_recorded.value: active sometime during the Persian period (539 - c. 330 BCE)
